title: Sonic Sculptor: Audio-Reactive Head Deformation Studio
description: A floating LeePerrySmith head faces a BoomBox that emits visible sound waves. The user controls the BoomBox's frequency, amplitude, and pulse rate via sliders, which deform the head's geometry in real-time through vertex displacement. Users cycle through deformation modes, adjust material properties, and capture snapshots of their sculpted creations.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive audio-reactive head deformation studio.

SCENE SETUP: Place the LeePerrySmith head (scaled to roughly 2 units tall) at center-right of the scene. Place the BoomBox (scaled up ~150x from its tiny default size) at center-left, approximately 3 units away from the head, aimed toward it. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 5) with OrbitControls. Add a dark gradient background (deep navy to black). Lighting: one warm SpotLight from upper-left illuminating the head, one cool-toned PointLight near the BoomBox with a subtle emissive glow, and a dim AmbientLight.

CORE INTERACTIONS (7 steps with validation):
1. FREQUENCY SLIDER (0.5-10.0 Hz, default 2.0): Controls the spatial frequency of sine-wave vertex displacement on the head's geometry. Validate range.
2. AMPLITUDE SLIDER (0.0-0.5, default 0.1): Controls displacement magnitude. Validate non-negative and max 0.5.
3. PULSE RATE SLIDER (0.1-5.0, default 1.0): Controls how fast the deformation animates over time. Validate range.
4. DEFORMATION MODE BUTTON: Cycles through three modes — 'radial' (displacement along vertex normals), 'directional' (displacement toward BoomBox position), and 'noise' (Perlin-style random offset using sin combinations). Display current mode name on-screen.
5. HEAD MATERIAL TOGGLE: Cycles the head's material between original PBR, wireframe overlay (MeshStandardMaterial with wireframe=true blended), and a glossy chrome MeshStandardMaterial (metalness=1.0, roughness=0.05). Validate by showing material name.
6. WAVE VISUALIZATION TOGGLE: Toggle visible ring-shaped wave meshes (TorusGeometry rings) that pulse outward from the BoomBox toward the head, scaling and fading with distance. Rings should spawn at the pulse rate.
7. SNAPSHOT BUTTON: Captures renderer.domElement.toDataURL() and displays it as a thumbnail in a bottom gallery strip (max 4 thumbnails).

On each animation frame, clone or modify the head geometry vertices based on current frequency, amplitude, pulse rate, time, and selected mode. The BoomBox should subtly vibrate (oscillate position/rotation) proportional to amplitude. Build a styled HTML overlay panel on the left side for all controls with labeled sliders and buttons.
